origin.description: Commands that turn one character vector into another, in the GNU diff normal form.
origin.usage: ses(a, b, max.diffs = gdo("max.diffs"), warn = gdo("warn"))

arguments.name: a
arguments.text: The starting vector. Non-character values are coerced with as.character. NA is compared as the string NA.

arguments.name: max.diffs
arguments.text: Stop the quadratic search after this many differences and finish with the linear failover. -1 keeps the original search.

arguments.name: warn
arguments.text: Warn when the difference limit is hit.

origin.details: Matches are left out. A change is NcM, a delete is NdK, and an insert is KaM. Positions are 1-based.
origin.value: A character vector. It is empty when a and b match.
origin.example:
a <- letters[1:6]
b <- c("b", "CC", "DD", "d", "f")
ses(a, b)

translation.description: The same GNU commands. The script comes from the myersmba port of src/diff.c.

arguments.name: a
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings, numbers, or bools. None is missing and is compared as NA.

arguments.name: max_diffs
arguments.text: Difference limit. None uses the diffobj.max.diffs option, which starts at 50000. A negative value keeps the original search.

arguments.name: warn
arguments.text: Warn when the limit is hit. None uses the diffobj.warn option.

translation.details: A string is one element, not a sequence of characters. Numbers are formatted with R's as.character rules. The result is a list of strings.
translation.value: A list of strings, empty when the vectors match.
translation.example:
from diffobj import ses
a = list("abcdef")
b = ["b", "CC", "DD", "d", "f"]
print("\n".join(ses(a, b)))
